text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have persistent vomiting and chest pain; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain is related to your meals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

Based on your history of forceful vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption, followed by sudden choking, coughing, and chest pain, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of an esophageal rupture. This is a life-threatening emergency that typically requires immediate surgical intervention.
